## Labor Relations and Collective Bargaining {.section-slide data-background-color="#102a43"}

## Federal Bargaining Rights, by Executive Order

:::: {.timeline .lr-eo}
<div class="tl-step accent-step"><span class="tl-year">March 27, 2025</span><span class="card-heading">Executive Order 14251</span><p>Excludes most federal agencies from collective bargaining, citing national security</p></div>
<div class="tl-step fragment"><span class="tl-year">2025</span><span class="card-heading">Unions sue</span><p>A district court blocks the order; agencies stop honoring contracts where they can</p></div>
<div class="tl-step fragment"><span class="tl-year">Feb. 26, 2026</span><span class="card-heading">Ninth Circuit</span><p>Lifts the injunction. The order is "grounded in national security"; the lawsuit goes on</p></div>
::::

::: {.question-bar .fragment}
If a president can end bargaining by executive order, what does a union contract in government protect?
:::

::: source-line
Exec. Order No. 14251, Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs (Mar. 27, 2025); *AFGE v. Trump* (9th Cir. Feb. 26, 2026).
:::

## Unions Are Strongest in Government

::: {.stat-row}
<div class="stat"><span class="stat-number">32.9%</span><p>of public-sector workers are union members</p></div>
<div class="stat fragment"><span class="stat-number">5.9%</span><p>of private-sector workers are</p></div>
<div class="stat fragment"><span class="stat-number">37.8%</span><p>in local government: teachers, police, firefighters</p></div>
:::

::: source-line
U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Union Members — 2025 (Feb. 18, 2026).
:::

## Who Can Bargain Depends on Who You Work For

::::::: {.system-cols .lr-regimes}
::: system-col
[Private and nonprofit]{.card-heading}

<p>National Labor Relations Act; may strike</p>
:::

::: system-col
[Federal]{.card-heading}

<p>Civil Service Reform Act; no strikes; pay isn't bargained</p>
:::

::: {.system-col .lr-idaho}
[State and local]{.card-heading}

<p>Each state decides. **Idaho:** firefighters and teachers bargain; state agency employees don't</p>
:::
:::::::

## Bargaining, Step by Step

:::::::::: {.pathway .lr-path}
::: pathway-step
[Who's in the unit]{.card-heading}

<p>Employees with a shared "community of interest"</p>
:::

::: pathway-arrow
→
:::

::: pathway-step
[Negotiate]{.card-heading}

<p>Some subjects must be bargained; some stay with management</p>
:::

::: pathway-arrow
→
:::

::: {.pathway-step .accent-step}
[Live with the contract]{.card-heading}

<p>Grievances, for the life of the contract</p>
:::
::::::::::

::: {.jd-note .fragment}
If talks stall: mediation, then fact-finding, then binding arbitration.
:::

## Grievances End with a Neutral

:::::::::: {.pathway .lr-path .lr-griev}
::: pathway-step
[Supervisor]{.card-heading}

<p>Employee and union steward</p>
:::

::: pathway-arrow
→
:::

::: pathway-step
[Department head]{.card-heading}

<p>A written appeal</p>
:::

::: pathway-arrow
→
:::

::: pathway-step
[Top management]{.card-heading}

<p>HR or the agency head</p>
:::

::: pathway-arrow
→
:::

::: {.pathway-step .accent-step}
[A neutral]{.card-heading}

<p>An arbitrator or hearing officer decides</p>
:::
::::::::::

::: {.takeaway .fragment}
Tonight's case is decided at the last step.
:::

## Activity: Should They Bargain? {.activity-slide data-background-color="#176b87"}

::: activity-prompt
Each group gets one workforce.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="pm-stay lr-stay">
<div class="pm-stay-card"><span class="pm-stay-tag">Group 1</span><p>Employees at an Idaho state agency, who can't bargain today</p></div>
<div class="pm-stay-card"><span class="pm-stay-tag">Group 2</span><p>Caseworkers at a Boise nonprofit</p></div>
<div class="pm-stay-card"><span class="pm-stay-tag">Group 3</span><p>Nurses at a VA medical center, where EO 14251 ended bargaining</p></div>
</div>
```

::: jd-questions
1.  Should they be able to bargain? Give one reason for and one against.
2.  What's the first thing they'd want on the table?
:::

::: activity-close
8 minutes in groups, then each group reports
:::

## Fair and Inclusive Workplaces {.section-slide data-background-color="#102a43"}

## Organizational Justice

::::::: {.system-grid .roomy-grid .lr-justice}
::: system-item
[Distributive]{.card-heading}

<p>Were the outcomes fair?</p>
:::

::: system-item
[Procedural]{.card-heading}

<p>Was the process fair?</p>
:::

::: system-item
[Interactional]{.card-heading}

<p>Were people told why, and treated with respect?</p>
:::
:::::::

::: {.question-bar .fragment}
Think of a decision at work that felt unfair. Which kind of justice was missing?
:::

## Two Kinds of Sexual Harassment

::::: {.compare .jd .roomy .jd-cols}
::: compare-side
[Quid pro quo]{.card-heading}

<p>A job benefit is tied to submitting to sexual conduct</p>
:::

::: {.compare-side .accent}
[Hostile work environment]{.card-heading}

<p>Conduct severe or pervasive enough to change the conditions of work</p>
:::
:::::

::: {.question-bar .fragment}
Does it matter whether the harasser meant it?
:::

## What the Employer Needs in Place

:::::::::: {.pathway .lr-path .lr-employer}
::: pathway-step
[A policy]{.card-heading}

<p>Written, and communicated</p>
:::

::: pathway-arrow
→
:::

::: pathway-step
[Training]{.card-heading}

<p>Especially for supervisors</p>
:::

::: pathway-arrow
→
:::

::: pathway-step
[Ways to report]{.card-heading}

<p>Including one that bypasses the supervisor</p>
:::

::: pathway-arrow
→
:::

::: {.pathway-step .accent-step}
[Prompt action]{.card-heading}

<p>Investigate, discipline in proportion, no retaliation</p>
:::
::::::::::

## Activity: The List {.activity-slide data-background-color="#176b87"}

::: activity-prompt
You work in HR for a city. Your best friend works for the city too, has a baby on the way, and closes on a house next month.
:::

::: activity-prompt
A memo lists the employees who will be laid off in 30 days. Your friend is on it.
:::

::: jd-questions
1.  Do you tell your friend?
2.  Is that fair to everyone else on the list?
:::

::: activity-close
5 minutes in groups, then each group gives its answer
:::
